verdict_basis: No product defect found. The fresh local Ubuntu exact MVP8 rerun could not complete on this host: all attempts abort in phase1 gateway init with MVP3_BACKEND_DISCONNECTED on authority/a because authority/a's synchronous native-owner init (CPU-bound, ~10-12 CPU-seconds, freezes the headless main loop including ENet servicing) exceeds the ENet default peer-timeout window (~16s) under heavy host CPU oversubscription (load 14-17 on 12 CPUs, foreign long-running Godot simulations of an unrelated project consuming 4+ cores for 2.5+ days, cpu.pressure some 17-24%). The identical accepted-code control tests fail at the identical init point on the same frozen tree, proving the failure is host-level, not MVP8-product-level: tests/integration/test_v0_mvp_7_graphical_reconnect.py (accepted MVP7, no MVP8 diff code) and tests/integration/test_v0_mvp_6_graphical_construction.py fail with the same 'native owner init authority/a: MVP3_BACKEND_DISCONNECTED' signature (authority/a stall ticks 360-376, authority/b healthy). strace observation of the stalled authority/a shows a live poll/nanosleep main loop after init completes (no deadlock); the gateway aborts first on the ENet PEER_DISCONNECTED event while the authority is still inside its synchronous init. The identical signature was documented by the Windows R1 verifier as host-level degradation (same tick 361 freeze), and the identical tree+engine passes 3/3 on GitHub ubuntu-latest CI with xvfb. Frozen CI evidence was re-downloaded and independently re-verified from raw files (57/57 independent checks green, artifact digest sha256:0d4eab2d... re-confirmed live). Therefore the gap is environment/runner-side only; per instruction it is NOT classified as a product defect and does not trigger FIX_REQUIRED.
